<!-- getting-started -->

# Getting started

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/getting-started

# Getting started

OpenUI installs framework-native components as source files. There is no
runtime package, no provider, and no version lock-in: once a component is in
your project, it is your code.

## Requirements

- [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.1 or newer (the beta CLI runs on Bun).
- Tailwind CSS v4 in the target project.
- One of React 18+, Svelte 5, Astro 5+, or Vue 3.3+.

> The beta ships TypeScript sources directly. A Node-compatible build is
> planned before the first stable release. See [Contributing](https://openui.dev/docs/contributing)
> for the current limitations.

## Install the CLI

```bash
bun add -g @openui/cli
```

Or run it without installing:

```bash
bunx @openui/cli --help
```

## Initialize your project

Run `init` from the project root:

```bash
openui init
```

The command detects your framework from `package.json` and writes
[`openui.json`](https://openui.dev/docs/configuration). If detection is inconclusive it writes
`"framework": "auto"` and tells you to choose one:

```bash
openui init --framework svelte --css src/app.css
```

## Add a component

```bash
openui add button
```

The CLI reads the registry, resolves the right item for your framework and
language, and writes the component into `src/components/ui`. Existing files are
never replaced unless you pass `--overwrite`. Use `--dry-run` first when you
want to see the plan:

```bash
openui add button --dry-run
```

## Use it

### React

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";

export function SaveBar() {
  return <Button type="submit">Save changes</Button>;
}
```

### Svelte

```svelte
<script>
  import Button from "$lib/components/ui/button.svelte";
</script>

<Button variant="secondary">Save changes</Button>
```

### Astro

```astro
---
import Button from "../components/ui/button.astro";
---

<Button type="submit">Save changes</Button>
```

### Vue

```vue
<script setup>
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";
</script>

<template>
  <Button variant="secondary">Save changes</Button>
</template>
```

## Verify the setup

```bash
openui validate
```

This checks `openui.json`, the registry index, every referenced item, and that
each install target stays inside your project. Run it in CI.

## Next steps

- Read [Configuration](https://openui.dev/docs/configuration) for every `openui.json` field.
- Learn the [CLI](https://openui.dev/docs/cli) and its safety guarantees.
- Browse the [Button](https://openui.dev/docs/components) API.
- Set up [theming](https://openui.dev/docs/theming) with Tailwind CSS v4.

---

<!-- configuration -->

# Configuration

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/configuration

# Configuration

OpenUI uses exactly one configuration file: **`openui.json`**. There is no
`openui.config.ts` and no JavaScript configuration API, so the same file is
readable by humans, CI, editors, and the JSON Schema at
`https://openui.dev/schema.json`.

## Example

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://openui.dev/schema.json",
  "framework": "auto",
  "typescript": true,
  "tailwind": {
    "css": "src/styles/global.css",
    "prefix": ""
  },
  "aliases": {
    "components": "@/components",
    "ui": "@/components/ui"
  },
  "registry": {
    "url": "https://openui.dev/registry"
  }
}
```

## Fields

### `$schema`

Optional. Points editors at the JSON Schema for autocomplete and validation.
`openui init` writes the canonical URL.

### `framework`

One of `"react"`, `"svelte"`, `"astro"`, `"vue"`, or `"auto"`.

- `"auto"` (default) detects the framework from dependencies and telltale files.
- An explicit value always wins and disables detection.

Detection reads `package.json` dependencies in order of evidence strength,
then checks for framework files such as `src/App.svelte`, `src/App.vue`, or
`src/pages`. If nothing is conclusive, commands that need a framework fail with
an actionable error telling you to set the field or pass `--framework`.

### `typescript`

Boolean. `true` (default) installs TypeScript variants (`.tsx`, typed props).
`false` installs JavaScript variants where they exist.

React items ship both `.tsx` and `.jsx` files; the CLI picks one. Svelte,
Astro, and Vue sources are written in plain JavaScript with JSDoc types so the
same file works in both TypeScript and JavaScript projects. This is why those
framework sources avoid `lang="ts"`.

### `tailwind.css`

Path to the project's global Tailwind CSS entry file, relative to the project
root. Used to place CSS artifacts and to render accurate guidance.

### `tailwind.prefix`

Optional Tailwind class prefix, for example `"tw-"`. Use `""` for no prefix.
The prefix is not rewritten in component sources during the beta; components
assume an un-prefixed setup.

### `aliases.components`

The import alias for your shared component directory.

### `aliases.ui`

The import alias for installed OpenUI primitives. Registry targets use the
`{ui}` token, which expands to this directory.

Aliases are resolved in this order:

1. `compilerOptions.paths` from `tsconfig.json` or `jsconfig.json`,
   including wildcard entries such as `"@/*": ["./src/*"]`.
2. The common `@/` → `src/` convention.

Paths are always interpreted relative to the **project root** — the directory
containing `openui.json` — never relative to the current working directory.

### `registry.url`

Either an `https://` URL serving `index.json` and `r/*.json`, or a filesystem
path (absolute, or relative to the project root). Filesystem registries are
useful for vendoring, air-gapped environments, and registry development.

## Discovery

The CLI searches for `openui.json` in the current directory and then walks up
parent directories, like Git. This lets a monorepo keep one config at the root
while packages run commands from their own directories.

An explicit `--config path` skips discovery. If that path does not exist, the
command fails instead of silently falling back to discovery.

## CLI flags

Flags override values for a single invocation **without rewriting the file**:

```bash
openui add button --framework vue --registry ./vendor/registry
```

`init` is the only command that writes configuration. It refuses to replace an
existing file unless you pass `--force` (or confirm an interactive prompt), and
it warns that unknown fields are lost when overwriting.

## Unknown fields

Unknown fields produce warnings, not errors, and are preserved in memory.
Because the file is plain JSON, deleting a field is a deliberate edit; the CLI
never rewrites your config to normalize it.

A misspelled field gets a suggestion:

```
Unknown field "tailwind.cs". Did you mean "tailwind.css"? Preserved but ignored.
```

## Validation

`openui validate` checks the config and the configured registry. `openui init`
validates the config it generates before writing it, so it cannot create an
invalid file by construction.

---

<!-- cli -->

# CLI

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/cli

# CLI

The `openui` CLI initializes projects, installs components, inspects the
registry, and builds or validates registries.

```bash
openui <command> [options]
```

Global options work with every command:

| Option        | Description                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `--cwd <dir>` | Run as if the process started in `<dir>`.   |
| `--help`      | Show help. Use `openui help <command>` too. |
| `--version`   | Print the CLI version.                      |

## `openui init`

Writes `openui.json`.

```bash
openui init
openui init --framework vue --css src/app.css --no-typescript
```

| Option                                          | Description                       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `--framework <react\|svelte\|astro\|vue\|auto>` | Override detection.               |
| `--typescript` / `--no-typescript`              | Choose the target language.       |
| `--registry <url-or-path>`                      | Registry location.                |
| `--css <path>`                                  | Tailwind entry file.              |
| `--components-alias <path>`                     | Shared components alias.          |
| `--ui-alias <path>`                             | UI primitives alias.              |
| `--force`                                       | Overwrite an existing config.     |
| `--yes`                                         | Accept prompts non-interactively. |

Refuses to overwrite without `--force` (or a confirmed prompt).

## `openui add <component…>`

Installs one or more components, including registry dependencies.

```bash
openui add button
openui add button --dry-run
openui add button --overwrite
```

| Option                             | Description                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `--dry-run`                        | Print the plan; write nothing.     |
| `--overwrite`                      | Replace existing files.            |
| `--yes`                            | Accept prompts non-interactively.  |
| `--framework <name>`               | Override the configured framework. |
| `--typescript` / `--no-typescript` | Override the configured language.  |
| `--registry <url-or-path>`         | Override the configured registry.  |
| `--config <path>`                  | Use a specific `openui.json`.      |

Existing files are skipped and reported unless `--overwrite` is passed.
Registry targets containing `..` are rejected, so an item can never write
outside the project root.

## `openui list`

Lists components in the configured registry.

```bash
openui list
openui list --json
```

`--json` prints the raw registry index for scripts.

## `openui diff <component>`

Compares installed files with the registry and reports `missing`, `in-sync`, or
`modified`, with a compact line diff for modified text files. Use it before
upgrading a component you have customized locally.

## `openui validate`

Validates `openui.json`, the registry index, and — for filesystem registries —
every referenced item and target. Remote registries validate their index
locally; items are validated when installed.

```bash
openui validate
```

This is the command to run in CI.

## `openui build`

Maintainer command. Reads `registry/openui-registry.json` at the repository
root, inlines sources from `packages/<framework>/src`, generates JSX siblings
for React TypeScript sources, and writes `registry/index.json` plus
`registry/r/*.json`.

```bash
openui build
```

It prunes generated items that are no longer referenced, so the output is
reproducible and reviewable. See [Registry](https://openui.dev/docs/registry).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                              |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | Success.                                             |
| `1`  | Validation, configuration, registry, or usage error. |

Errors are printed to stderr with a suggested next step where possible.
Unknown options and commands fail rather than being ignored.

## Safety model

1. Load and validate configuration before touching disk.
2. Fetch and validate every registry item.
3. Expand targets and reject path escapes.
4. Compute a write plan (`create`, `overwrite`, `skip`).
5. Apply the plan, honoring `--dry-run` and `--overwrite`.

No command mutates `openui.json` except `init`, and `init` never silently
replaces an existing file.

<!-- components -->

# Components

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/components

# Components

OpenUI components are source files, not a runtime library. Each one:

- uses only framework primitives and Tailwind CSS utilities;
- has **no OpenUI runtime dependency** and no third-party runtime dependency;
- ships a plain class-joining helper instead of `clsx` or `tailwind-merge`
  (variants are disjoint, so class conflicts do not arise);
- defaults to `type="button"` so a button inside a form never submits by
  accident.

## Button

The beta ships one reference component, `button`, implemented natively for all
four supported frameworks.

### Props

| Prop        | Type                                                         | Default   | Description                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `primary \| secondary \| outline \| ghost \| danger \| link` | `primary` | Visual emphasis.                       |
| `size`      | `sm \| md \| lg \| icon`                                     | `md`      | Control height and horizontal padding. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   | Stretch to the container width.        |
| `type`      | `button \| submit \| reset`                                  | `button`  | Native button type.                    |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   | Native disabled state.                 |

Every other native attribute (`aria-*`, `onClick`, `form`, …) is forwarded to
the underlying `<button>`.

### Variants

| Variant     | Use                                             |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `primary`   | The single highest-emphasis action on a screen. |
| `secondary` | Supporting action on a subtle surface.          |
| `outline`   | Bordered action in dense or neutral layouts.    |
| `ghost`     | Borderless action in toolbars.                  |
| `danger`    | Destructive or irreversible action.             |
| `link`      | Inline action styled like a link.               |

### Sizes

`sm` is 32px tall, `md` is 40px, `lg` is 48px, and `icon` is a 40×40 square.

### Accessibility

- Uses a real `<button>` element, so keyboard and screen-reader behavior is
  native.
- Includes a visible `focus-visible` ring with offset.
- Disabled buttons use both `disabled` and `pointer-events-none` plus reduced
  opacity.
- `type` defaults to `button` to avoid accidental form submission.
- For icon-only buttons, pass an accessible name:

```tsx
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Close dialog">
  <CloseIcon aria-hidden="true" />
</Button>
```

## Usage by framework

### React

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";

<Button variant="danger" size="lg" onClick={remove}>
  Delete project
</Button>;
```

### Svelte

```svelte
<script>
  import Button from "$lib/components/ui/button.svelte";
</script>

<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={save}>Save</Button>
```

Svelte content is passed as a snippet:

```svelte
<Button>
  {#snippet children()}
    <span>Save</span>
  {/snippet}
</Button>
```

### Astro

```astro
---
import Button from "../components/ui/button.astro";
---

<Button variant="secondary" type="submit">Save</Button>
```

Astro content goes into the default slot.

### Vue

```vue
<script setup>
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";
</script>

<template>
  <Button variant="ghost" @click="close">Close</Button>
</template>
```

Vue content goes into the default slot.

## Customizing

Components live in your project after installation. Edit them directly. Use
`openui diff button` to see what changed before pulling a registry update, and
`openui add button --overwrite` only when you intend to replace local edits.

Add new variants or sizes by editing the component's class maps. Keep variants
disjoint — for example, do not give two variants background utilities that can
conflict — so the simple join helper remains correct.

<!-- registry -->

# Registry

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/registry

# Registry

A registry is a static directory — or an HTTP prefix — with two parts:

```
registry/
├── index.json              # catalog: components, metadata, item locations
├── r/
│   ├── button-react.json   # self-contained install item
│   ├── button-svelte.json
│   ├── button-astro.json
│   └── button-vue.json
└── openui-registry.json    # maintainer manifest (not served)
```

`index.json` is the only file the CLI fetches to browse. Installing one
component fetches its item once, because every file's content is inlined.

## Index format

```json
{
  "name": "openui",
  "version": "0.1.0-beta.0",
  "homepage": "https://openui.dev",
  "components": {
    "button": {
      "title": "Button",
      "description": "A framework-native button.",
      "frameworks": {
        "react": { "item": "r/button-react.json" },
        "svelte": { "item": "r/button-svelte.json" }
      },
      "meta": {
        "variant": [{ "name": "primary", "description": "High-emphasis action." }]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`meta` is documentation data: variants, sizes, and props used by this site and
by the generated LLM docs.

## Item format

```json
{
  "name": "button",
  "framework": "react",
  "version": "0.1.0-beta.0",
  "description": "A framework-native button.",
  "dependencies": [],
  "registryDependencies": [],
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "packages/react/src/button.tsx",
      "target": "{ui}/button.tsx",
      "type": "component",
      "content": "…"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Target tokens

| Token                | Expands to                               |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `{ui}`               | Resolved `aliases.ui` directory.         |
| `{components}`       | Resolved `aliases.components` directory. |
| `{css}`              | Directory of `tailwind.css`.             |
| `{name}` / `{style}` | Reserved for future registry features.   |

Targets are always project-root relative. Any target containing `..` is
rejected, even if the resolved path would remain inside the project.

### Dependencies

- `dependencies` lists npm packages the consumer must install. OpenUI
  components keep this empty by design.
- `registryDependencies` lists other registry items to install first. The CLI
  resolves them depth-first and deduplicates.

## Building

Component sources in `packages/<framework>/src` are canonical. The manifest at
`registry/openui-registry.json` maps each component to its sources:

```json
{
  "name": "button",
  "sources": {
    "react": [
      {
        "path": "packages/react/src/button.tsx",
        "target": "{ui}/button.tsx",
        "type": "component",
        "languageVariants": true
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Then run:

```bash
bun run registry:build
```

The command:

1. reads each package version from `packages/<framework>/package.json`;
2. inlines sources and generates a `.jsx` sibling for React TypeScript files;
3. validates every generated item against the registry schema;
4. writes deterministic JSON and prunes stale items.

The generated registry is committed for the beta so it can be served
statically. Never edit `registry/index.json` or `registry/r/*.json` by hand.

## Serving

Any static host works. Point `registry.url` at the directory that contains
`index.json`:

```json
{ "registry": { "url": "https://openui.dev/registry" } }
```

For development, use a filesystem path:

```json
{ "registry": { "url": "./vendor/registry" } }
```

## Validating

```bash
bun run registry:validate
```

For filesystem registries, validation fetches every item referenced by the
index, checks name/framework consistency, and expands every target to prove it
stays inside the project. Remote registries validate the index locally; items
are validated when installed.

## Publishing a version

Registry item versions track their framework package version. The beta uses
Changesets in pre-release mode:

```bash
bun run changeset
bun run version-packages
bun run registry:build
bun run registry:validate
```

Keep the registry index version in `registry/openui-registry.json` aligned with
the package version you are publishing.

---

<!-- theming -->

# Theming

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/theming

# Theming

OpenUI components are styled with plain Tailwind CSS utility classes. There is
no CSS-in-JS runtime, no theme provider, and no stylesheet shipped by the
registry. Your Tailwind build already sees the classes because the components
are source files inside your project.

## Tailwind CSS v4 setup

If your project does not have Tailwind yet, follow the official Tailwind v4
installation for your framework. The essential pieces are:

1. Add `tailwindcss` and your framework's Tailwind plugin.
2. Import Tailwind in your global CSS:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```

3. Make sure `openui.json` points at that file:

```json
{
  "tailwind": { "css": "src/styles/global.css", "prefix": "" }
}
```

No additional OpenUI import is required.

## What the components use

The Button uses core Tailwind utilities and the built-in `zinc` and `red`
palettes:

- Surfaces: `bg-zinc-900`, `bg-zinc-100`, `bg-transparent`.
- Text: `text-white`, `text-zinc-900`, `text-zinc-50`.
- Borders: `border-zinc-300`, `border-zinc-700`.
- Focus: `ring-zinc-400`, `ring-zinc-600`, with `ring-offset-2`.

Because these are standard utilities, they work in any Tailwind v4 project
with no token configuration.

## Dark mode

Dark styles are written with Tailwind's `dark:` variant. Tailwind v4 defaults
to the `prefers-color-scheme` strategy. To switch manually, define a custom
variant in your global CSS:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
```

Then toggle a `dark` class on `<html>`.

## Brand tokens

For a brand palette, map utilities to your own CSS variables with Tailwind v4's
`@theme`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --color-brand: oklch(0.55 0.2 255);
  --color-brand-foreground: white;
}
```

Edit the installed component to use them:

```diff
-  primary: "bg-zinc-900 text-white hover:bg-zinc-800",
+  primary: "bg-brand text-brand-foreground hover:bg-brand/90",
```

Remember that components are your source: edit them directly, and use
`openui diff button` before accepting a registry update.

## Local overrides

Every component accepts a `class`/`className` prop and merges it last:

```tsx
<Button className="rounded-full px-8">Pill</Button>
```

Because variants are disjoint and the merge is a simple join, your utility
comes later in the class list. For conflicting utilities, Tailwind's generated
CSS order — not class-attribute order — decides the winner. Prefer overriding
the component's variant map when you need a guaranteed conflict-free change.

## Accessibility

Focus rings and disabled styles are part of the base classes. If you customize
them, keep:

- a visible focus indicator with sufficient contrast;
- a non-color-only disabled cue where possible;
- at least a 40×40px target for icon-only buttons (the `icon` size).

---

<!-- contributing -->

# Contributing

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/contributing

# Contributing

OpenUI is a Bun monorepo. Component sources are canonical; the registry and
documentation are generated from them.

## Layout

```
packages/core        Config schema, validation, framework detection, registry contracts
packages/cli         The `openui` command
packages/react       Canonical React sources
packages/svelte      Canonical Svelte sources
packages/astro       Canonical Astro sources
packages/vue         Canonical Vue sources
registry/            Manifests (hand-written) + generated index/items
apps/docs            Astro documentation site and generated LLM docs
scripts/             Verification, schema, and LLM docs generators
.agents/skills/      Instructions for coding agents working in this repo
```

## Setup

```bash
bun install
bun run verify
```

`verify` is the single command that must pass before a pull request. It runs
formatting, linting, type checks, tests, registry generation and validation,
schema and LLM docs generation, and a production docs build.

## Formatter and linter

The project uses the **oxc toolchain**:

- `oxfmt` for formatting (TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, CSS, Markdown, and
  framework files through its bundled Prettier support);
- `oxlint` for linting JavaScript and TypeScript.

There is no separate "Cox" formatter or linter package on npm. The original
request referred to this toolchain; the names `oxfmt`/`oxlint` are used in
documentation so contributors can find the real packages. Configuration lives
in `oxfmt.json` and `.oxlintrc.json`.

**Known limitation:** `oxlint` does not lint `.svelte`, `.astro`, or `.vue`
component files. Those files are covered by compiler tests in each framework
package (`svelte/compiler`, `@astrojs/compiler-rs`, `vue/compiler-sfc`), which
fail on syntax and template errors.

Commands:

```bash
bun run format        # write formatting
bun run format:check  # verify formatting
bun run lint          # lint JS/TS
bun run lint:fix      # apply safe lint fixes
```

## Tests

```bash
bun test
```

Tests live next to the code they cover:

- `packages/core/test` — config validation, detection, registry contracts.
- `packages/cli/test` — argument parsing, commands, safety behavior, and
  cross-framework installs against a generated registry.
- `packages/<framework>/test` — component behavior or compilation.
- `apps/docs/test` — LLM documentation validation.

Add a regression test with every behavior change. CLI tests use temporary
directories and never touch the repository.

## Documentation

Documentation pages are canonical Markdown in `apps/docs/content/docs` and
`apps/docs/content/docs/frameworks`. The LLM-friendly copies under
`apps/docs/public/llms*` are generated:

```bash
bun run llms:generate
bun run llms:validate
```

Do not edit generated files by hand. Update the Markdown source and regenerate.
When you add a page, also add it to `REQUIRED_SLUGS` in
`scripts/lib/docs.ts` if it must always exist.

## JSON Schema

`apps/docs/public/schema.json` is generated from the core config schema:

```bash
bun run schema:generate
```

Never hand-edit the schema; change `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts` first.

## Changesets

Every user-facing change needs a changeset:

```bash
bun run changeset
```

Choose the affected packages and a bump type, and describe the change for the
changelog. The repository is in Changesets pre-release mode for the beta, so
versions look like `0.1.0-beta.0`. Publishing is manual:

```bash
bun run version-packages
bun run registry:build
bun run verify
bun run release
```

See `.changeset/config.json`. `@openui/docs` is private and ignored.

## Commits

Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```
feat(components): add badge
fix(cli): reject empty component names
docs: explain alias resolution
chore: bump oxfmt
```

Keep commits focused. Run `bun run verify` before pushing.

## Beta limitations

- The CLI runs on Bun and ships TypeScript sources; a Node-compatible build is
  planned before the first stable release.
- Component packages publish source files, not compiled distributions.
- `oxlint` does not lint framework component files (see above).
- Tailwind class prefixes are configured but not rewritten in component
  sources.
- The registry is committed and served statically from the docs deployment.

---

<!-- frameworks/react -->

# React

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/react

# React

OpenUI ships native React components with typed props. There is no runtime
package: `openui add` writes the component into your project.

## Install

```bash
openui init --framework react
openui add button
```

The CLI installs `.tsx` by default. For a JavaScript project:

```json
{ "typescript": false }
```

or per command:

```bash
openui add button --no-typescript
```

React items include both variants in the registry; the CLI selects one based on
`typescript`.

## Import

With the default `@/` alias and a `tsconfig.json` mapping:

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
```

The destination comes from `aliases.ui` plus `compilerOptions.paths`. If you
use relative imports instead, import from the generated path:

```tsx
import { Button } from "./components/ui/button";
```

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";

export function DeleteProject({ onConfirm }: { onConfirm: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={onConfirm}>
      Delete project
    </Button>
  );
}
```

In the Next.js App Router, event handlers require a Client Component. Add
`"use client"` at the top of the file that uses interactive props; purely
visual buttons can stay server-rendered.

## Forms

`Button` defaults to `type="button"`, so it does not submit a form unless you
ask it to:

```tsx
<form action={save}>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
  <Button variant="ghost" type="reset">
    Reset
  </Button>
</form>
```

## Props

```tsx
interface ButtonProps extends React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> {
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "ghost" | "danger" | "link";
  size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "icon";
  fullWidth?: boolean;
}
```

All native attributes are forwarded. See [Components](https://openui.dev/docs/components) for
variant and size guidance.

## Styling

The component uses standard Tailwind utilities. Pass `className` to extend it:

```tsx
<Button className="rounded-full">Pill</Button>
```

## Type checking

The installed file is plain TypeScript with no imports beyond `react` types, so
it type-checks under `strict` mode. If your project does not use the automatic
JSX runtime, configure `"jsx": "react-jsx"` in `tsconfig.json`.

## Testing

Render with your preferred test runner. A minimal React Testing Library check:

```tsx
render(<Button variant="danger">Delete</Button>);
expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete" })).toHaveClass("bg-red-600");
```

---

<!-- frameworks/svelte -->

# Svelte

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/svelte

# Svelte

OpenUI ships native Svelte 5 components. The installed file uses runes and
snippets — no legacy slots, stores, or runtime package.

## Install

```bash
openui init --framework svelte
openui add button
```

The component is written in plain JavaScript with JSDoc types, so the same file
works in TypeScript and JavaScript Svelte projects. There is no `lang="ts"` to
break JavaScript tooling.

## Import

With SvelteKit's default `$lib` alias:

```svelte
<script>
  import Button from "$lib/components/ui/button.svelte";
</script>
```

If your project uses a different alias, update `aliases.ui` in `openui.json`
so install destinations match your imports.

## Usage

```svelte
<script>
  import Button from "$lib/components/ui/button.svelte";

  let saving = $state(false);
</script>

<Button variant="secondary" disabled={saving} onclick={() => (saving = true)}>
  {saving ? "Saving…" : "Save"}
</Button>
```

Svelte 5 uses `onclick` (not `on:click`) for native event attributes.

## Children

Content is passed as a snippet:

```svelte
<Button variant="danger">
  {#snippet children()}
    <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" />
    Delete
  {/snippet}
</Button>
```

Text between the tags also renders when no explicit snippet is supplied.

## Forms

The component defaults to `type="button"`. Opt into submission:

```svelte
<form method="POST">
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>
```

## Props

```js
/** @typedef {"primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "ghost" | "danger" | "link"} ButtonVariant */
/** @typedef {"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "icon"} ButtonSize */
```

| Prop        | Default   |
| ----------- | --------- |
| `variant`   | `primary` |
| `size`      | `md`      |
| `fullWidth` | `false`   |
| `type`      | `button`  |

Remaining props (including `aria-*`, `disabled`, and `class`) are forwarded to
the `<button>`. `class` is merged with the generated classes.

## Styling

Components use standard Tailwind utilities. Tailwind v4's Svelte integration
discovers classes in `.svelte` files automatically. Pass `class` to extend:

```svelte
<Button class="rounded-full">Pill</Button>
```

## Type checking

The file is plain JavaScript with JSDoc, so `svelte-check` understands its
props without a TypeScript SFC. Keep `checkJs` off if your project does not
type-check JavaScript files; the component remains valid either way.

## Testing

The repository compiles this component with `svelte/compiler` and renders the
server output in tests. Use a similar smoke test to ensure a customized
component still compiles.

<!-- frameworks/astro -->

# Astro

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/astro

# Astro

OpenUI ships native `.astro` components. They render to static HTML with zero
client-side JavaScript unless you add interactivity yourself.

## Install

```bash
openui init --framework astro
openui add button
```

The component is plain JavaScript frontmatter with JSDoc types, so it works in
both TypeScript and JavaScript Astro projects.

## Import

Astro components are default exports; the local name is yours to choose:

```astro
---
import Button from "../components/ui/button.astro";
---

<Button type="submit">Save</Button>
```

The installed component has no named exports, so always use a default import.

## Usage

```astro
---
import Button from "../components/ui/button.astro";

const items = await getItems();
---

<div>
  <Button variant="secondary">Refresh</Button>
  <Button variant="danger" data-action="delete">Delete</Button>
</div>
```

## Slots

Content inside the tag goes to the default slot:

```astro
<Button variant="ghost">
  <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" />
  Delete
</Button>
```

## Interactivity

An Astro component is server-rendered. A `Button` with no client directive
renders HTML and consumes no JavaScript. To handle clicks, either use a tiny
inline script:

```astro
<Button data-confirm>Delete</Button>

<script>
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-confirm]").forEach((button) => {
    button.addEventListener("click", () => {
      if (!confirm("Delete this item?")) return;
      button.closest("form")?.submit();
    });
  });
</script>
```

or render your framework's island component (`client:load`) when the
interaction needs state.

## Forms

The component defaults to `type="button"`. For native form submission:

```astro
<form method="POST" action="/api/save">
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>
```

## Props

| Prop        | Default   |
| ----------- | --------- |
| `variant`   | `primary` |
| `size`      | `md`      |
| `fullWidth` | `false`   |
| `type`      | `button`  |

Unknown props — including `aria-*`, `disabled`, and `class` — are spread onto
the `<button>` element. `class` is merged with the generated classes.

## Styling

The component uses standard Tailwind utilities. Astro's Tailwind v4
integration scans `.astro` files. Pass `class` to extend:

```astro
<Button class="rounded-full">Pill</Button>
```

## Testing

The repository compiles this component with `@astrojs/compiler-rs` in tests, so
syntax and template errors fail CI. A production Astro build is the strongest
end-to-end check for a customized component.

<!-- frameworks/vue -->

# Vue

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/vue

# Vue

OpenUI ships native Vue 3 single-file components. The installed file uses
`<script setup>` and plain JavaScript with runtime prop validation, so it works
in both TypeScript and JavaScript projects.

## Install

```bash
openui init --framework vue
openui add button
```

## Import

```vue
<script setup>
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";
</script>
```

Vite resolves `@/` through your alias configuration. If you use a different
alias, update `aliases.ui` in `openui.json` so install destinations match.

You can also register the component globally:

```ts
import { createApp } from "vue";
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";
import App from "./App.vue";

createApp(App).component("Button", Button).mount("#app");
```

## Usage

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";

const saving = ref(false);

async function save() {
  saving.value = true;
  try {
    await fetch("/api/save", { method: "POST" });
  } finally {
    saving.value = false;
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <Button variant="secondary" :disabled="saving" @click="save">
    {{ saving ? "Saving…" : "Save" }}
  </Button>
</template>
```

Events use Vue's `@click` binding. Native attributes such as `aria-*`,
`disabled`, and `class` fall through to the root `<button>` element and classes
are merged automatically.

## Slots

Content goes into the default slot:

```vue
<Button variant="ghost">
  <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" />
  Delete
</Button>
```

## Forms

The component defaults to `type="button"`. Opt into submission:

```vue
<form method="POST" @submit.prevent="save">
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                                         | Default   |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| `variant`   | `primary \| secondary \| outline \| ghost \| danger \| link` | `primary` |
| `size`      | `sm \| md \| lg \| icon`                                     | `md`      |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   |
| `type`      | `button \| submit \| reset`                                  | `button`  |

`variant` and `size` include runtime validators; an unknown value warns in
development and falls back visually to the default class set.

## Styling

Components use standard Tailwind utilities. Pass `class` to extend:

```vue
<Button class="rounded-full">Pill</Button>
```

Tailwind v4's Vue integration scans `.vue` files.

## Testing

The repository compiles this SFC with `vue/compiler-sfc` and server-renders it
with `vue/server-renderer`, so template errors and invalid props fail CI.
Mount the component with Vue Test Utils for interaction tests in your own
project.
